# Configure the MCP Sidecar

This page describes how to configure the MCP Sidecar on Kubernetes. You register AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, define which tools each agent can call, and set up human approval. To learn how the sidecar governs tool calls, refer to [Govern tool access with the MCP Sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access).

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Workflow

Complete the following steps:

1. Register AI agents.
1. Register MCP servers.
1. Send tool calls through the sidecar.
1. Define tool policy.
1. Configure human approval.
1. Verify the configuration.

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed with the [`ai.agent.image`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-agent-image) Helm value set. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).
- [Transparent proxy](/consul/docs/connect/proxy/transparent-proxy/k8s) mode for AI agent pods. Consul rejects the agent's proxy configuration in any other mode. The Helm chart enables transparent proxy by default, so do not set `consul.hashicorp.com/transparent-proxy` to `false` on agent pods.
- An AI agent that uses an MCP client.
- One or more MCP servers that use a supported transport. In-mesh servers run in the service mesh. External servers need a terminating gateway.

## Register AI agents

Annotate the pod template of each AI agent with the `ai-agent` role. Consul injects the MCP Sidecar into the pod.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="5">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: ai-agent
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The sidecar uses the defaults in the [`AgentConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/agentconfig) resource. Use the annotations to override a default for one pod. Each port must not conflict with the application port or the Envoy proxy port, `20000`.

| Setting | Purpose | Default | Annotation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MCP connectivity port | The loopback port the agent sends tool calls to, at `/mcp` | `15101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-mcp-port` |
| Agent interceptor port | The loopback port of the governance interceptor in the MCP Sidecar. Consul rejects every tool call when nothing listens on it. | `21101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-interceptor-port` |
| Human approval server port | The loopback port of the approval server that receives approval requests | `16101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-port` |
| Human approval timeout | How long Consul waits for a verdict before it rejects the call | `60s` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-approval-timeout` |

The sidecar listens on a Unix domain socket by default. In local development, or where a shared socket volume is unavailable, set `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-addr` to switch the listener to TCP. Refer to [Kubernetes annotations and labels](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/annotation-label) for details.

## Register MCP servers

Annotate the pod template of each in-mesh MCP server with the `mcp-server` role. Consul registers the service with the `mcp-server` role and adds an MCP router filter to the pod's inbound Envoy listener.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="5">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: mcp-server
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The registration uses the defaults in the [`McpServerConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/mcpserverconfig) resource. Use the annotations to override a default for one pod.

| Setting | Default | Annotation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP transport | `streamable-http` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-transport` |
| MCP path | `/mcp` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-path` |
| MCP protocol version | `2025-03-26` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-protocol-version` |

The `McpServerConfig` resource also sets `interceptorPort`, the TCP port the MCP server container listens on inside the pod. It defaults to `21102`.

To reach an MCP server outside the mesh, route the call through a terminating gateway. Refer to [Configure external credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection/configure).

## Send tool calls through the sidecar

Configure the agent's MCP client to send every tool request to the MCP listener on loopback:

```plaintext
http://localhost:15101/mcp
```

If you changed the MCP connectivity port, use that port instead. The agent does not call MCP servers directly. Service intentions decide which server and tool each call can reach.

A tool name with a `<server>__<tool>` prefix names the MCP server. Without that prefix, the server is the destination of the intention that allows the call.

To carry the user's identity to an MCP server, also add the server as an explicit upstream of the agent. Upstreams decide the on-behalf-of token audiences. They do not authorize tool calls. Refer to [On-behalf-of token audiences](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity/configure-oauth-clients#on-behalf-of-token-audiences).

## Define tool policy

Allow each tool call with a service intention. The intention names the MCP server as the destination and the agent as the source. Its allow permission must set the HTTP path to exactly `/mcp` and match the `x-mcp-tool` header, whose value is the tool name. Consul ignores permissions that use a different path or that omit an `x-mcp-tool` match.

1. Set the MCP server's protocol to `http`. The default protocol is `tcp`, and Consul rejects a layer 7 (L7) permission for a TCP destination. Refer to [service defaults](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/service-defaults).
1. Create the intention.

The following example allows `billing-agent` to call the `billing.lookup` tool on `billing-tools`:

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Kubernetes">

<CodeBlockConfig filename="billing-tools.yaml">

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceDefaults
metadata:
  name: billing-tools
spec:
  protocol: http
---
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceIntentions
metadata:
  name: billing-tools
spec:
  destination:
    name: billing-tools
  sources:
    - name: billing-agent
      permissions:
        - action: allow
          http:
            pathExact: /mcp
            header:
              - name: x-mcp-tool
                exact: billing.lookup
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

```shell-session
$ kubectl apply --filename billing-tools.yaml
```

</Tab>
<Tab heading="HCL">

```hcl
Kind = "service-defaults"
Name = "billing-tools"
Protocol = "http"
```

```hcl
Kind = "service-intentions"
Name = "billing-tools"
Sources = [
  {
    Name = "billing-agent"
    Permissions = [
      {
        Action = "allow"
        HTTP = {
          PathExact = "/mcp"
          Header = [
            {
              Name  = "x-mcp-tool"
              Exact = "billing.lookup"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

To allow several tools in one permission, match `x-mcp-tool` with `Regex`. A `Regex` match is not a general regular expression. Consul expands only one anchored alternation of literal tool names, such as `^(hotel\.search|flight\.search)$`. Any other pattern is one literal tool name, so `^billing\..*$` matches a tool named `billing..*`.

## Configure human approval

On Kubernetes, Consul installs the human approval filter on every AI agent. Approval runs only for tool requests that include the `x-mcp-hitl` header. Requests without the header skip approval.

For a request that needs approval, Consul sends an approval request to the approval server on port `16101` and waits for a verdict. Consul rejects the call in either of the following cases:

- No verdict arrives before the approval timeout, which defaults to `60s`.
- The approval server is missing or unreachable.

To change the timeout for every agent, set `spec.defaults.hitl.approvalTimeout` in the `AgentConfig` resource. To change it for one pod, set the `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-approval-timeout` annotation.

## Verify the configuration

1. Send a tool discovery request from the agent to `localhost:15101/mcp`, and confirm that the response lists the tools the agent is allowed to see.
1. Call an allowed tool, and confirm that the MCP server receives the request.
1. Call a tool that no intention allows, and confirm that Consul rejects the call.
1. Call a tool with the `x-mcp-hitl` header and no approval, and confirm that Consul rejects the call after the approval timeout.
